solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: School teacher hours subject to revision

indicators.note: something subject to revision is going to be reworked, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: A teacher's timetable at some school is about to be revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subject to revision' rearranges TEACHER HOURS. CHARTERHOUSE is an English private boarding school in Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Charterhouse is a famous English public school, so it is an example of a school.

clue.text: Someone a man isn't when out of sorts, bizarrely

definitions.text: Someone a man isn't when out of sorts, bizarrely

parts.words: Someone a man isn't when out of sorts, bizarrely
parts.note: the idiom says someone off colour is 'not his usual self', so the clue describes the person he fails to be

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'he is not his usual self' means a man is unwell or out of sorts; the clue asks for the person he is not.

clue.text: Bird predicting bad weather at dawn?

definitions.meaning: a small European songbird of the thrush family with a rust-coloured tail
the rhyme 'red sky in the morning, shepherd's warning' says a red beginning to the day means rain is coming

explanation.definitionFit: The redstart is a songbird, and a red start to the day foretells foul weather in the old rhyme.

clue.text: Make designs and such like with end of brush

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and such like

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word brush

explanation.surface: An artist decorates with a brush and other such tools.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut designs into a surface with acid or a sharp tool.

clue.text: Anglo-Catholic building with tall spire

definitions.meaning: the wing of the Church of England keeping Catholic ritual and doctrine
a place of worship whose steeple is lofty, read literally as a phrase

explanation.definitionFit: High Church names the ritualist Anglo-Catholic tradition, and read literally it is a lofty place of worship.

clue.text: Set up partial market in US to pool resources

indicators.note: Set up says the hidden letters are read backwards
partial says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arranging a stall at an American market is a way of sharing costs.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Set up' reverses: ETINU runs through 'market in US' and reads upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together, as partners do when they combine their funds.

clue.text: Period certain to result in wipe-out

parts.note: an era is a period of history
sure means certain

explanation.surface: An age that is bound to end in total destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: An erasure is the act of rubbing something out completely, a wiping out.

clue.text: Final draught ready to go?

parts.note: a last drink taken by someone about to set off home from the pub

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the last drink before departing, a draught being a drink of beer.

clue.text: Workers go all out to ensure its success

definitions.text: Workers go all out to ensure its success

parts.words: Workers go all out to ensure its success
parts.note: 'go all out' seems to mean try hard, but here means every worker walks out of work

explanation.definitionFit: A stoppage in which workers across all industries down tools together succeeds only if everyone leaves work.

clue.text: Travelling with foreign coin bearing central cross

indicators.note: the rearranged coin carries the next word in its centre
foreign suggests something strange or altered, so the letters of coin are rearranged

parts.note: cross means angry, mad

explanation.surface: A traveller carries a foreign coin stamped with a cross in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' turns COIN into NOIC; 'bearing central' puts MAD into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people move from place to place, so it is a synonym for wandering or roving.

clue.text: Forbidding one to make a face

parts.note: grim means stern or forbidding
an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.walkthrough: 'Forbidding' looks like a verb meaning banning, but it is the adjective, grim.
explanation.definitionFit: To grimace is to twist the features in disgust or pain, pulling a face.

clue.text: Fast-moving ships, lots of them

definitions.meaning: a large group of vessels under one command

explanation.definitionFit: Fleet means swift as an adjective and a navy's body of vessels as a noun.

clue.text: Dodge back after school for the timetable

indicators.note: after places the reversed dodge behind the school abbreviation
back means the word for dodge is read in reverse

parts.note: to elude is to dodge

explanation.surface: Skipping off after lessons to check the bus times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodge' looks like a verb about skipping school, but it supplies the word to be turned round; SCH is a standard dictionary abbreviation for school.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule is a plan listing times of events, which is what a timetable is.

clue.text: Strangely tender name, appropriately

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of the next two words come out in an odd order

explanation.surface: A loving nickname, rearranged, fits itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges TENDER NAME; 'appropriately' signals that the fodder also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An endearment is a term of affection such as darling, a tender name for someone.

clue.text: Whistle-blower working under me gets popular vote

parts.note: a ref, short for referee, blows the whistle in a game

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are being worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An informant who reports to me wins a public ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whistle-blower' suggests an informant, but it is a sports official. 'working' rearranges UNDER ME into ERENDUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A referendum puts a single question to the whole electorate, a vote of the people.

clue.text: Average woman gets taken in

indicators.note: taken in says the name sits inside the word Average

explanation.surface: An ordinary woman is easily fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a woman's given name, as crosswords often clue names by woman or girl.

clue.text: Leading member of the quadrupeds

parts.note: fore means at the front, leading
a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: The top animal among four-footed creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading member' seems to mean a chief among animals, but it is a front leg.
explanation.definitionFit: A forelimb is a front leg, the foremost limb of a four-footed animal.

clue.text: Ham with German wine

definitions.meaning: a joint of meat from a pig's leg, the knuckle end
a white wine from the Rhineland

explanation.definitionFit: Hock is both the pig's lower leg joint cut as ham and the British name for Rhine wine.

clue.text: Run with the pack, like Conservative at his best

parts.note: someone at his best is on form

explanation.surface: A Tory at the peak of his career just follows the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to follow the crowd, doing what everyone else does.

clue.text: Bet he's getting terrible cold without these

definitions.text: Bet he's getting terrible cold without these

indicators.note: terrible suggests something has gone badly wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone without blankets is sure to catch a nasty chill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges BET HE'S with COLD; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets and blankets keep a sleeper warm, so without them he catches cold.

clue.text: Marx brother takes on Lance

parts.note: Harpo was one of the Marx Brothers comedy team
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comedian takes on a man called Lance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lance' looks like a man's name, but it is a verb meaning spear.
explanation.definitionFit: To harpoon is to spear, as to lance is to pierce with a pointed weapon.

clue.text: Start to get exhausted, so don't finish race?

definitions.meaning: a race cut short, read literally as a run made short

explanation.definitionFit: To run short is to begin to lack something, and literally a run made short leaves a race unfinished.

clue.text: Where to stop mentioned in letter

definitions.meaning: a place to stay the night on a journey
the word used for H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is lodging for travellers, and it is also the radio code word for the letter H.

clue.text: Dread taking time off — it's not right

indicators.note: taking with off says a letter is removed
off with taking says the letter is removed from the word for dread

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, dread

explanation.surface: Fearing to take a break is a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a mistake, something that is wrong.

clue.text: Headless statuette, reminder of sword-fight?

indicators.note: headless says the first letter is cut off the word for the statuette

parts.note: the Oscar is the Academy Award statuette

explanation.surface: A broken trophy recalls a duel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oscar statuette loses its first letter to leave SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left by a wound, so a duellist's scar recalls the fight.

clue.text: One in twelve has a job with the French

parts.note: a post is a job
le is French for the

explanation.surface: One of a dozen workers gets a position in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Jesus chose twelve apostles, so an apostle is one of the twelve.

clue.text: Australian hen shelters in a hot wind

indicators.note: shelters says the word for the hen goes round the next word

parts.note: chook is Australian slang for a chicken

explanation.surface: An Aussie chicken hides from a scorching wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is fodder, not a link: CHOOK shelters IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinook is a warm dry wind that blows down the eastern Rockies.

clue.text: Soldiers barred, we're told, but top brass welcome here!

parts.note: the military are soldiers collectively

indicators.note: we're told says the word for barred is heard, not written

parts.note: barred means banned

explanation.surface: Soldiers are banned, yet senior officers are welcomed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top brass' seems to mean senior officers, but it means the best brass players.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimental ensemble is full of brass players, so skilled brass players are welcome there.
